title: Walking along the beach
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What have you read that came back to you months later?

groups.heading: Learning that is not an obligation

lines.text: I said that a lot had happened in the last two weeks and I wanted to reflect on last year and this year: what is it about stand-up and about reading and learning that changes our perspective? When we read, how do we extract meaning from the books? How is it relevant in your life? How does it change you?

It is not an obligation, I said. We are programmed that way in education, which is the problem I have with my own kids' school. Guys, don't let school make you feel the concept of learning is an obligation. If you don't want to read something, don't read it.

A student said: the things that we read and talk about sometimes come back months later. This morning I was thinking about something we read in an earlier book, and I'm at a point in my life where I can apply it. It doesn't go in one ear and out the other when we talk about it over and over and apply it.

I said that when I read, I read five or six books at once, and that you find interconnecting things between them, which is exciting. I gave a metaphor: imagine you are walking along a beach, and that is passing the pages of a book.

Every step along an empty beach you are looking down for specific things that jump out at you, I said: maybe white shells, maybe brown, something you have never found before. How frequently do you take those walks? That is constantly learning and not having limitations.

A student said: this book is not something I would have read on my own, because I had preconceived notions about the person. It has been revealing, and inspirational, because when you have challenges, you look at the challenges he faced, a person who doesn't take no for an answer and figures out a way.
Which nuggets from the last book have you put in your pocket?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write what you read last that has stayed with you.
Write two books you could read side by side to find the connections.
Write what you read only because you felt you had to.
Write how often you take a walk on the beach.

check.q: What did I say learning should not be?
What did I compare passing the pages of a book to?
What did a student say about what we read and talk about?
choices: It can come back months later

recap: Learn without obligation. Read widely and find the connections. Keep the nuggets in your pocket.
